answer: The economy spends reputation the way a market spends money: sparingly and against verified performance, so Sybil inflation is filtered out before it can compound into a decisive advantage. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a voyage as the anchor of the cost.
